# Dormant control-sector first study

This informed study is not a blind benchmark. Five original sources distinguish
three zero-qubit positive controls, a one-bit dormant counterexample and its
direct monomorphic negative control. No source repair or maximum-size quantum
case was generated. The first plan remains `execution: not run`; separate actual
observations preserve every command, exit status and full stdout/stderr.

The unused generic body containing `flip(ctrl q)` accepted, although the same
closed call in an ordinary function refused with the native computational-basis
sector diagnostic. X is unitary but does not preserve those sectors. This is a
missing dormant control request, not evidence for a false Unitary effect label.
The three zero-width controls accepted; empty Ctrl axes make their sector
condition vacuous. Those results alone cannot validate the one-bit refusal.
Exact scalar phase and distinct logical owner trees still remain relevant.

The accepted scalar, closed `hold[scalar]`, mixed-owner and dormant-X cases
reported 19, 21, 20 and 19 native decisions respectively, with zero independent
requests. All report an unpinned checker, no entry and unproved source
preservation. Native validity of the ordinary roots did not discharge the
unused body's control obligation. The separate after-integration predictions
are requirements, not observed successes.

Observed HEAD `739c24860698234c5489941f8c55447535d2b793` included the dirty closed-Op
repair later committed in #413. CLI SHA-256
`a94f242cb191f31fd6b7fb35ec71c8e607d5f68d5fec89107d1edc8855389f45`
and kernel SHA-256
`54c9d60b80f67217abd95c8fe6ec1c06aa262e142d5e6db30f46a20cb90faf07`
identify the observed executables. This is not a clean commit-to-binary build
attestation. The 17 original Rust snapshots are scoped provenance, not complete
build inputs or a source/native/runtime preservation proof. Every input,
executable and scoped source remained stable during capture; the preceding
Meaning studies remained unchanged. Recorded times are not performance bounds.

One deterministic USTAR/gzip archive preserves all 40 original files / 635,383
bytes, including source, manifests, snapshots, predictions and actual
observations. Its manifest binds complete byte/mode
inventories and compressed/expanded identities. The existing 80-member, 5 MiB
expanded and 2 MiB compressed bounds remain unchanged. Only regular mode-0644
members with canonical local paths and fixed metadata are retained.

The bounded retention reader never executes recorded commands or source and
does not extract files to the filesystem. This history does not complete
generic materialization, all dormant expressions, QS/PR/quantitative RS/EXACT,
an Issue or a release. Primitive/local-Op control requests, owner-frame and
clean-workspace obligations retain their separate concrete checking duties.
